{{Quote|Freia lures the Neimoidians to Imynusoph, whose natives seem peaceable, though Freia has become rather high-handed in her dealings (Freia and Chorus: 'Bow Down to the Stars').|Excerpts from the program for the [[2 ABY/Legends|38:2:13]] premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
In the [[Opera/Legends|opera]] ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'', the '''Imyni''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Imynusoph/Legends|Imynusoph]]. The [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] treated them presumptuously while enlisting their aid in exacting revenge on her rivals, the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] [[Thoax Osaax|Thoax]] and [[Farge Osaax]]. As a result, when Kallea ordered the Imyni to bind the Osaaxes while she sprung her trap in a [[Temple of Imynusoph|temple]] on Imynusoph, the natives instead turned on all the offworlders, leading to a climactic [[Battle on Imynusoph|battle]].

==Society and culture==
The Imyni were a [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that, in the [[Musician/Legends|composer]] [[Trebian Shullos]]'s [[Opera/Legends|opera]] ''[[The Kallea Cycle]]'', lived on the rumored treasure [[Planet/Legends|world]] [[Imynusoph/Legends|Imynusoph]], which in reality eventually became a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']]<ref name="TEA" /> [[Kallea sector/Legends|Kallea sector]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}} &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Imynusoph system/Legends|Imynusoph system]]</ref> In the opera, the Imyni were depicted as seemingly peaceable.<ref name="TEA" />

==History==
{{Quote|Freia orders the Imyni to bind the Neimoidians, but the Imyni turn on all the outworlders ''[&hellip;]''|Excerpts from the program for the 38:2:13 premiere of ''The Kallea Cycle''|<ref name="TEA" />}}
[[File:The_Kallea_Cycle.jpg|thumb|right|300px|In the opera ''The Kallea Cycle'', the Imyni turned on Freia Kallea (center; depicted by [[Vessa Brentioch]]) after she treated them presumptuously.]]
In ''The Kallea Cycle'', which depicted the [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Freia Kallea/Legends|Freia Kallea]] overcoming various difficulties in [[Star map/Legends|charting]] the [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]-spanning [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]] [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|hyperlane]] between [[3705 BBY/Legends|3705 BBY]] and [[3694 BBY]], Kallea attempted to exact revenge on her rivals, the [[Neimoidian/Legends|Neimoidians]] [[Thoax Osaax|Thoax]] and [[Farge Osaax]], by setting a trap for them on Imynusoph. In the process, she enlisted the aid of the Imyni, though she treated them in a presumptuous manner&mdash;as represented by the opera's [[Music/Legends|composition]] "[[Bow Down to the Stars]]." Kallea lured the two Osaaxes to a [[Temple of Imynusoph|great temple]] on Imynusoph, where she revealed herself at a banquet and then ordered the world's natives to bind the Neimoidians.<ref name="TEA" />

At that point, however, the Imyni instead turned on all the offworlders present. At the same [[Time/Legends|time]], a band of [[Dug/Legends|Dug]] and [[Gran/Legends|Gran]] [[Mercenary/Legends|thugs]] hired by the Osaaxes for protection arrived on Imynusoph, as did a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] planet [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal]] led by the Human [[Sival Brentioch]], Kallea's patron and member of the [[Noble/Legends|noble]] [[House Brentioch]]. During the climactic [[Battle on Imynusoph|battle]] that ensued, the Imynusoph temple was set [[Fire/Legends|ablaze]], and in the opera's denouement, the Osaaxes were arrested and Kallea and Brentioch departed Imynusoph.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Imyni were introduced in the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="TEA" />
